newsitem.title: UK: GOLF-JOHANSSON WINS ENGLISH, BOOSTS RYDER BID.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-JOHANSSON WINS ENGLISH, BOOSTS RYDER BID.

text.p: Per-Ulrik Johansson virtually assured himself a second successive Ryder Cup place on Sunday when he won the English Open by two strokes.
The 30-year-old Swede carded a closing five-under-par 67 for a 269 total, 19 under par, to beat compatriot Dennis Edlund for his fourth victory on the European Tour.

The triumph hoisted Johannson from 10th to third place in the Ryder Cup rankings with 304,945 points, close to the forecast target figure for a top-10 qualifying spot for the match against the Americans at Valderrama in September.

"The place is looking really good now. If I get into the team this time maybe I'll be able to handle the situation a bit better," said Johansson, who won his debut match for Europe with Germany's Bernhard Langer at Oak Hill in 1995 but then lost his singles to Phil Mickelson.
"I was as nervous as hell on the first tee then. It would be nice to win a singles this time," he said.
Edlund, 31, posted a 69 for 271, a shot ahead of American Jay Townsend and young Englishman Steve Webster.
The leader for the first two rounds, England's Roger Chapman, shared fifth place a further stroke back with countryman David Howell.
The overnight leader, English club professional Gary Emerson, soon hit trouble with a run of four bogeys in five holes, finishing with a 75 to slip back to joint 10th on 276.
Scotland's veteran Ryder Cup campaigner Sam Torrance brought himself back into the reckoning for Valderrama by finishing joint seventh after a 67.
Fellow Scot Colin Montgomerie, the European number one, cheered himself with a 67 finish but had to settle for a total eight shots adrift of Johansson in joint 12th spot.
He was one shot better than Spaniard Jose Maria Olazabal, whom he will meet in the first round of the eight-man Andersen Consulting European zone match play event on Monday.
Johansson chipped in for birdie on the 10th and then followed up with a 12-foot eagle putt on the long 12th to virtually sew up the event.
"The chip-in on the 10th was the turnaround and the eagle on 12 the big turnaround. I absolutely killed a five-iron into the green and that's a tribute to my coach David Whelan.
Whelan is from the school of top teacher David Leadbetter.
"The key to winning was down to my swing. I enjoy playing when I can trust it and David got me swinging shorter and wider, which worked great.
"This tournament's been good to me. I've been second, fourth, sixth and now a win," Johansson said."
"At the end of 1995 I was on the point of giving up the game," revealed Edlund. "My sponsors persuaded me to carry on and I'm glad they did."
He won 72,210 pounds ($115,000)to ensure he keeps his playing card for 1998.
